chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about two men who shared a slave girl, so they married her to a man. Then the man bought one of the two shares. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She becomes prohibited to him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying a slave girl when her owners are partners and the husband buys one share?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the specific juristic ruling for a *mukatab* or partially enslaved woman owned by two partners, establishing that if her husband purchases one of the two shares, she becomes fully prohibited (*haram*) to him. This ruling highlights the distinct Shia legal principle that marriage to a partially enslaved woman is contingent upon the husband owning her entire share, and acquiring the remaining share does not necessarily validate the existing bond in the same way as full ownership, thereby preventing the *haram* status from being lifted by mere consolidation. The narration underscores the precision of early Shia jurists in distinguishing between the rights of ownership and the validity of marital bonds in cases of shared property.
